question: Should native Codex turns admit operator-allowlisted, already-installed and enabled `workspace-directory` plugins and make `marketplaceKinds` plus stable remote plugin IDs part of OpenClaw's supported app-server contract?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but only maintainers can authorize the durable expansion from curated plugins to organization-scoped capabilities and own its compatibility floor.

options.title: Approve constrained workspace support
options.body: Accept exact catalog IDs, require installed and enabled state, expose only owned accessible apps, retain default-deny policy, and never install workspace plugins.

options.title: Retain curated-only support
options.body: Reject workspace admission until maintainers choose a different boundary or the upstream contract is considered stable enough to support.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained workspace support
recommendation.body: Accept exact catalog IDs, require installed and enabled state, expose only owned accessible apps, retain default-deny policy, and never install workspace plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history ties the canonical native-plugin inventory and policy path to this owner, who also merged the prior adjacent marketplace work.
